name: Invitation Homes Inc.
moat_justification: Real local-density and scale economies in maintenance, leasing and builder sourcing, but rent is a market price, leases are annual with no switching costs, SFR is dominated by mom-and-pop owners, and measured returns are low (ROE 2.67% in 2021 to 6.17% in 2025 in fundamentals.json; roic_proxy and gross margin are not computed for 2018-2025 in fundamentals.json).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 8.7x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.5%) vs bull-case tier C (10.4%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Quality SFR landlord, moat 4/10 — at $26.77 it does not clear 15% on any scenario (weighted IRR 9.0%, IV@15% $13.79 vs $26.77); it would need ~$13.79 to clear the hurdle.
moat_for: Largest SFR platform (~109k homes owned/JV/managed) with local density in 16 markets lowering per-home maintenance and turn costs
Vertically integrated acquire-renovate-lease-manage platform built since 2012
Builder partnerships / ResiBuilt and construction lending give sourced supply at scale
Structural housing shortage and rent-vs-own cost gap support 97.1% Q2 2026 same-store occupancy
moat_against: No network effects or tenant switching costs — annual leases, rent set by the local market
SFR supply is overwhelmingly fragmented mom-and-pop stock; scale is efficiency, not a barrier
AMH and other institutional landlords can replicate the model with capital
Property-tax, insurance and maintenance cost inflation largely uncontrollable
